hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=-x$

Under this transformation, some points on the triangle map to another point which is no longer on the triangle. The triangle is *not symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A right triangle mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The right triangle has a point at negative eight, negative four, a point at four, negative four, and a point at four, six. The equation y equals negative X is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show where the points of the triangle's image will be after being reflected across the graphed line. The endpoints of the dotted lines are outside of the current pre-image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over the $x$-axis

Under this transformation, some points on the triangle map to another point which is no longer on the triangle. The triangle is *not symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A right triangle mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The right triangle has a point at negative eight, negative four, a point at four, negative four, and a point at four, six. Dotted lines show where the points of the triangle's image will be after being reflected across the x axis. The endpoints of the dotted lines are outside of the current pre-image.

hints.content:
Neither symmetry applies to the triangle.

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=-x$ | No
Reflective symmetry over the $x$-axis | No
